sentences.text: Nakanectes bradti is a short-necked elasmosaurid distinguished by possessing only 39 to 42 cervical vertebrae, a count much lower than in most other members of its group.
The genus name honors the Nakona people, also known as the Assiniboine, while the species name bradti commemorates the fossil hunter David Bradt.
This species was discovered in 2010 in Montana, United States, when hunter David Bradt found the fossil in November at the Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge.
The fossil specimen was partially destroyed by flooding before it could be fully recovered in 2011.
Researchers determined that Nakonanectes is a styxosaurine that exhibits convergent evolution with the South American Aristonectinae.
Nakanectes bradti is classified as an elasmosaurid plesiosaur from the late Cretaceous, belonging to the family Elasmosauridae and the parent group Elasmosaurinae within the class Reptilia.
Found in the Bearpaw Formation, Nakonanectes lived during the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian in the Western Interior Seaway, specifically between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
The presence of short-necked elasmosaurids in both North and South America suggests that this trait evolved independently in multiple locations.
